name: Ironpass Dock & Haul Full Kit
description: A harbor dockworker's full kit built for the wet, corrosive air of Meridian Harbor's lower loading decks. The outermost layer is a heavy-duty safety-orange weathershell jacket with sealed seams, acid-resistant coating, and a broad back panel printed with a white cargo handler designation number. The cuffs are wide enough to clear chrome forearm augments, with a secondary snap closure for a tighter seal in spray conditions. Beneath it sits a navy thermal henley with a reinforced neckline and flat-stitched seams to reduce pressure points under a harness rig. Cargo trousers in the same acid-resistant charcoal fabric as the jacket feature double-layered thigh panels, six external pockets with drain holes at the base, wide knee guards stitched in place with bright orange thread, and a reinforced crotch gusset for climbing and crouching. A name patch reading the wearer's dock assignment sits on the left chest of the jacket. Boots are heavy matte-black waterproof waders to mid-calf with steel toe caps, slip-resistant lug soles, and hook-and-bar lacing. A neoprene neck gaiter in navy rounds out the look, usually pulled down around the collar until the spray picks up.
functionality: Acid-resistant and waterproof outer shell, chrome-forearm-wide cuffs with secondary snap closure, drain-hole cargo pockets for wet environments, harness-compatible flat seams, reinforced knee and crotch panels for manual labor range of motion, steel-toe waterproof footwear, designation number printing for dock zone identification.
what_it_says: You move cargo for a living. You've been soaked through and dried out and soaked again so many times that your joints ache when the acid rain shifts direction. The designation number on your back is not a name but you've made peace with that. You know how to tie seventeen different load knots and you are not impressed by anyone who doesn't.
manufacturer: Ironpass WorkGear (street-adjacent industrial label, common in harbor districts)
story_hooks: A dockworker in this kit passes the players a cargo manifest folded inside their neoprene gaiter — the shipment listed doesn't match what was actually unloaded, and the designation number on their jacket places them at a berth that officially received nothing that night.

The acid-resistant coating on a particular jacket has been modified — someone has been using the outer shell fabric as a dead-drop surface, writing messages in a chemical ink that only appears under specific UV frequencies.
A dock worker is missing. All that's left at their assigned loading station is this kit, neatly folded, with the name patch cut out.

physical_description.visual_profile: Industrial workhorse aesthetic — blocky, utilitarian silhouette with high-visibility safety orange dominating. Broad shoulders, reinforced stance. Built to protect chrome and flesh alike in corrosive harbor spray. Reads as working-class functionality with no pretense of style.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately loose and layered for mobility and augmentation clearance. Jacket sits wide at shoulders with room for harness rigs. Cargo trousers have relaxed thigh taper with articulated knee guards. Waders add bulk at lower leg. Overall effect is armor-like, not body-conforming.
physical_description.primary_material: Acid-resistant synthetic composite (jacket and trousers outer), sealed-seam weatherproof shell. Navy thermal henley in brushed synth-wool. Neoprene gaiter. Waterproof rubberized wader material on boots with steel reinforcement.
physical_description.texture: Jacket has a waxy, industrial sheen with sealed seam ridging visible. Thermal henley is soft brushed pile. Trousers have a slightly stiff, treated finish. Boots are matte rubber with aggressive lug-sole texture. Neoprene gaiter has subtle ribbing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant safety orange (jacket, knee guards, stitching accent); charcoal gray (cargo trousers, boot base); navy (thermal henley, gaiter); white (designation number and cargo handler markings). High contrast for visibility in low-light dock conditions.
physical_description.closures: Sealed magnetic snaps on jacket cuffs with secondary friction-fit closure. Standard zipper down jacket front. Cargo trousers use friction-fit waistband with integrated belt loops. Boots feature hook-and-bar lacing system for rapid on/off.
distinctive_features: Wide cuff design to clear chrome forearm augments
Broad back panel with white cargo handler designation number
Six external pockets with drain holes
Personalized name patch (dock assignment) on left chest
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 (working class) — functional, durable, mass-produced by street-adjacent manufacturer. Investment in protection over appearance.
physical_description.cultural_context: Harbor dock worker, Meridian Harbor lower decks. Speaks to physical labor, augmentation tolerance, and familiarity with corrosive industrial environments. Wearer is likely chromed (forearm minimum), unionized or contract-based, operating in spray/acid-risk zones.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Jacket shows salt spray staining and acid spotting. Knee guards show scuffing. Boots heavily scuffed and salt-crusted. Thermal henley faded from repeated washing. Name patch worn at edges. Still functional — maintenance-patched rather than discarded.
